sources.dem: AWS Terrain Tiles (Mapzen/Tilezen Terrarium; USGS 3DEP on land, GEBCO/ETOPO1 bathymetry), https://registry.opendata.aws/terrain-tiles/ ; re-encoded, heights quantised to 0.5 m
sources.img: USGS The National Map: USGSImageryOnly (public domain), https://basemap.nationalmap.gov/arcgis/rest/services/USGSImageryOnly/MapServer

notes.dem: tiles/dem/{z}/{x}/{y}.png, 256 px Terrarium RGB, 0.5 m steps (B is 0 or 128)
notes.img: tiles/img/{z}/{x}/{y}.jpg, 256 px JPEG. A tile absent from this list was HTTP 404 upstream, blank white upstream, or failed; do not request it, use the parent. See imgUpstream404: whole zooms can be absent.
notes.imgPartlyTransparentNote: these tiles came as PNG with transparent pixels; in the mirrored JPEG those pixels are pure white, the colour upstream itself uses for no imagery (see imgWhiteNoData)
notes.imgBlankNote: tiles the service answered with HTTP 200 but that are white all over (>= 99.5 % of pixels, i.e. no imagery: open sea) are treated like 404: not written, not listed
notes.imgWhiteNoDataNote: USGS paints areas outside the imagery footprint PURE WHITE in its JPEG tiles (coast and open sea, every zoom from 11 up). Listed [x, y, percent white] for tiles with >= 0.5 % of pixels >= 248 on all channels (thinner slivers exist in other coastal tiles). JPEG tiles are mirrored byte-for-byte; PNG tiles are re-encoded with their transparent pixels also white. So in every mirrored tile pure white = no imagery: mask it (e.g. fall back to the parent tile or water colour).
notes.demSpikesNote: elevation tiles containing garbage pixels upstream (more than 250 m from the median of their 4 neighbours; values from -22 km to +4 km), [x, y, pixel count]. Kept as served (round trip <= 0.25 m): despike when meshing, e.g. replace by the neighbour median.
notes.demNoDataNote: elevation tiles with pixels at -32768 m (RGB 0,0,0 upstream = no data), [x, y, pixel count]; kept as served
